tx_maze_the.blurb: The Maze is a compact cluster of boulders on the East Spur of Hueco Tanks, packed with problems in a small space. The rock is the pocketed, hard igneous stone the park is famous for, and the climbing is all bouldering on holds, huecos and edges. Most of the problems fall between VB and V5, so there are plenty of warm-ups and moderate lines, with a thinner scattering of V6 to V9 and a couple of top-end projects. It is a common first stop on a day at the East Spur because the easy problems sit right beside the hard ones. Winter is the main climbing season here, when the desert sun is mild and friction is good.

ut_selfish_wall.blurb: Selfish Wall is a sandstone cliff in Indian Creek, sitting between Six Star and Hong Buttress, and it is all crack and trad climbing. The wall has faces pointing several directions, so you can chase the sun on a cold morning or hunt for afternoon shade in warmer weather. Routes are short to medium in length, and most land in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, with a smaller group at 5.9 and a few easier or harder lines. The approach follows a creek bed and a cairned path, and the road in can wash out, so allow a little extra walking. As elsewhere in the Creek, avoid climbing the sandstone when it is wet.

ut_the_optimator.blurb: The Optimator is an Indian Creek sandstone wall that sits with the Bridger Jacks on one side and the 4x4 Wall on the other. It is mostly traditional crack climbing, with the bulk of routes graded 5.10 through 5.12 and a handful of harder 5.13 lines plus a single aided route. The wall catches sun in the morning and stays in light until early afternoon, then the shade arrives, which makes it a good winter and spring stop and an easy pairing with a shadier wall nearby. Pitches run long here, so a 70 m rope is handy. The access road is rough for the first stretch and needs decent clearance. Avoid the rock after rain.

ut_shangri_la.blurb: Shangri La is a wall in the Jungle, on the Aquarius Plateau, at roughly 10,000 feet. The rock is volcanic tuff, and here it is regarded as the soundest stone in the whole Jungle, with some excellent cracks. Climbing is mostly trad with some sport and a few multi-pitch lines; grades cluster at 5.10 and 5.11, with a good number of 5.9s and a couple of 5.12s. Getting here means a long drive over rough roads beyond the main parking lot, then a short walk on a cairned trail. Summer afternoons bring thunderstorms, so start early, and fall is often the most pleasant time to visit.

ut_pipe_dream_the.blurb: The Pipe Dream is a big overhanging cave at the head of the Right Fork in Maple Canyon, a short hike up the trail. The conglomerate cobbles give steep, pumpy sport climbing on bolts. A few 5.11 and 5.12 routes serve as warm-ups, but most of the climbing here is 5.13 and 5.14, so it is a destination for strong climbers working hard lines. The horizontal roof keeps the cave shaded for most of the day, with a little early sun on the edges, and it stays mostly dry in a rainstorm. That shade makes it a favorite place to escape summer heat.

ut_sparks_wall.blurb: Sparks Wall is a sandstone cliff band in Indian Creek, reached by a dirt road that leads off toward Bridger Jack. Climbing is mostly trad crack, with grades that cluster in 5.10 and 5.11, a handful at 5.9 and a decent number of 5.12s, plus a few boulder problems at the base. The stone is softer than at some neighboring walls and sheds dust in wind or rain. A small group of routes face north, while more face southeast and take sun for much of a cool-season day. The trail in is well built and takes a modest amount of time. Stay off the rock when it is wet.

ut_stone_garden.blurb: Stone Garden is a quartzite crag in the high Uintas, reached from Kamas along the Mirror Lake Highway. The cliff is mainly sport climbing, with a few trad lines, and the rock is steep and sticky: expect face climbing on some routes and long overhanging lines on others. Sport grades mostly fall between 5.10 and 5.12, with a handful of easier and harder routes. The boulders sit only a minute's walk from the cliff and range from easy problems to hard highballs and compression lines. Because of the elevation, summer here runs much cooler than the Wasatch Front, which is the main reason people make the drive.
